expectations.text: A failing test is written before the implementation for each task in the section
expectations.evidence: Transcript shows tests/test_greetings.py was updated first, then `pytest -q tests/test_greetings.py` was run and failed with an ImportError, then after another test update it ran again showing '.F' with test_farewell failing (AssertionError: assert None == 'Goodbye, Ada!'), and only after that failing test was observed was src/greetings.py updated to implement farewell, followed by a passing run ('2 passed').
expectations.rubric: Red-before-green ordering per task: a failing test must be authored and observed to fail before its implementation. Ordering is a process property read from the transcript, not decidable from final state.

The full quality gate (`make check`, which covers tests beyond this section's own) is run once after all the section's tasks, not per task; the Red phase is confirmed with only the section-relevant test rather than the whole-suite gate
expectations.evidence: The Red-phase check used only the focused test — `pytest -q tests/test_greetings.py` — both when it failed on import and on assertion, never invoking `make check`. Only after farewell was implemented (both 1.1 and 1.2 done) did `make check` run, confirmed by the transcript command `pytest -q tests/test_greetings.py && make check && ...` showing '3 passed' before the commit — i.e., the whole-suite gate ran after the section's tasks were complete, not per individual task.
expectations.rubric: The whole-suite gate (`make check`) must run once after the section's tasks, while the per-task Red confirmation uses only the section-relevant test. This is an ordering/granularity property of the run, read from the transcript.
